$comment: Controls what gets generated, what the sweep looks for, and how dense it is. Edit this rather than the generator.
What `python -m tools.sweep` searches OpenStreetMap for, inside each area declared in
Selectors are a union, and each one is a set of OSM tags that must all match. Masts and
communication towers are tagged inconsistently between man_made=mast and man_made=tower,
so both are listed; taking only one of them misses real structures.
These three classes are deliberate. Buildings and wind turbines are the obvious things to
add and the two worst things to add blind: MSFS lights a lot of wind turbines itself, and
photogrammetry towers often come with their own beacons, so sweeping them doubles up. Add
them if you have checked your region in the sim, not before.
$min_marked_height_comment: Structures shorter than this are left unlit. FAA AC 70/7460-1 generally requires marking
from 200 ft AGL, and ICAO Annex 14 uses 45 m (about 150 ft) - lower it if you are outside
the United States and want the shorter masts.
This is also the frame-rate lever. Every marked structure costs one beacon plus a ring of
side lights per 150 ft below the top, so raising the floor thins the package fast.
$exclude_comment: OSM ids the sweep must never propose, as `type/id` - for example `way/12345678`.
This is where 'the sim already lights that one' gets recorded. A doubled or slightly
offset beacon reads worse than no beacon at all, and that judgement can only be made in
the sim, so it is recorded here once instead of being made again on every re-sweep.

limits.$comment: Hard ceilings. The build fails rather than silently shipping something that will tank the sim.
